patch.summary:
Choose Adobe Firefly only if your buying job matches “Adobe generative image/video — Free credits; Firefly Standard from ~$9.99/mo; Pro ~$19.99;” rather than Cursor's shape. Choose Cursor only if your buying job matches “AI-native code editor — Hobby free; Pro $20/mo; Teams Standard $40/user; Enterprise contac” rather than Adobe Firefly's shape. Workflow advantage: Adobe Firefly leans ai-image; Cursor leans ai-code. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Positioning: Adobe Firefly is Adobe generative image/video — Free credits; Firefly Standard from ~$9.99/mo; Pro ~$19.99; also bundled in Creative Cloud.; Cursor is AI-native code editor — Hobby free; Pro $20/mo; Teams Standard $40/user; Enterprise contact. Usage credits inside paid plans..
- Workflow coverage skew: Adobe Firefly-leaning ai-image vs Cursor-leaning ai-code.
- Researched limits: Adobe Firefly — Premium video/partner models consume credits even when standard images are unlimited on paid plans; Cursor — Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code.

Limitations — Adobe Firefly: Premium video/partner models consume credits even when standard images are unlimited on paid plans; Standalone pricing is easy to confuse with Creative Cloud Pro bundles; Cursor: Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code; Usage overage on Agent/frontier models can exceed $20 Pro.

Poor-fit cases: Adobe Firefly is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Premium video/partner models consume credits even when standard images are unlimited on paid plans · Cursor is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code · Avoid Adobe Firefly if you actually need Cursor's motion (AI-native code editor — Hobby free; Pro $20/mo; Teams Standard $40/user; Enterpr)
